question.prompt:
The circumference of the circle with center \(O\) is divided into \(12\) equal arcs, marked the letters \(A\) through \(L\) as seen below. What is the number of degrees in the sum of the angles \(x\) and \(y?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2014_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Equal arcs give equal angles at the center, so counting arc intervals will determine the angles in the two triangles.

[Figure 1](figures/2014_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

The \(12\) equal arcs divide the full turn at \(O\) into angles of
\[
\frac{360^\circ}{12}=30^\circ.
\]
From \(A\) through \(B,C,D\) to \(E\), there are four arc intervals. Thus \(\angle AOE=4\cdot30^\circ=120^\circ\). Since \(OA=OE\) are radii, triangle \(AOE\) has two equal base angles. Its angles sum to \(180^\circ\), so
\[
x=\frac{180^\circ-120^\circ}{2}=30^\circ.
\]
From \(G\) through \(H\) to \(I\), there are two arc intervals, giving \(\angle GOI=60^\circ\). Similarly, \(OG=OI\), so
\[
y=\frac{180^\circ-60^\circ}{2}=60^\circ.
\]
Therefore \(x+y=30^\circ+60^\circ=90^\circ\), choice C.
solutions.title: Central angles and equal radii
